issues.description: CHANGELOG entry name does not match the actual check directory/class name
issues.detail: The CHANGELOG entry calls it `compute_image_not_publicly_shared` and the PR description text says `compute_image_publicly_shared`. The code uses `compute_image_not_publicly_shared`. The PR title and description body both use the positive `publicly_shared` phrasing while the code uses the negated `not_publicly_shared`. Pick one name and use it everywhere — small thing, but the data (the identifier) is what flows through tooling, dashboards, and remediation links, so it must be exactly one string.

issues.description: Image listing silently swallows IAM-policy errors and reports the image as not publicly shared
issues.detail: In `_get_images`, when `getIamPolicy` raises (e.g. permission denied, as in the third fixture image), the code logs the error and then appends the Image with `publicly_shared=False`. That is a PASS for an image whose sharing state is unknown. The data structure is wrong: `publicly_shared` is a tri-state (yes/no/unknown) being squashed into a bool. Add an `iam_policy_known: bool` (or make the field `Optional[bool]`) and have the check skip or emit MANUAL/INFO when the policy could not be retrieved. As-is, a missing permission produces a false PASS — the worst failure mode for a security scanner.

issues.description: `_get_images` is one function doing four things; could be three small filters composed
issues.detail: The method interleaves: (1) paginate images.list, (2) per-image getIamPolicy, (3) scan bindings for allAuthenticatedUsers, (4) construct Image. Each is a stateless transform over a list. Splitting into `_list_images_for_project`, `_image_iam_policy`, and `_is_publicly_shared(policy) -> bool` would make each piece independently testable and the top-level loop one short comprehension. Right now the bindings scan is buried inside two `try` blocks and a `while`, which is the sort of code where future bugs hide.

issues.description: `publicly_shared` is a derived flag; storing the raw members would be more honest data
issues.detail: The Image model stores only a bool. The richer, more reusable shape is `public_members: list[str]` (or the full bindings) and let the check compute `bool(public_members)`. The PR description itself says the service adds `public_members` — but the code stores only the boolean. With `public_members`, future checks (specific role-based exposure, audit reporting, evidence in `status_extended`) become trivial without re-fetching IAM policy. Data dominates: store the data, derive the predicate.

issues.description: Test fixture monkey-patches `getIamPolicy` but does not exercise the error path through the real service
issues.detail: `mock_get_image_iam_policy` sets `side_effect = Exception("Permission denied")` for image 3, and `compute_service_test.py` then asserts image 3 has `publicly_shared=False`. That test is locking in the buggy behavior described above (unknown == PASS). Once the tri-state fix lands, this assertion must change. Flagging so the fix and the test move together.

issues.description: Bare `except Exception` with manual traceback-line formatting repeated across the service
issues.detail: Both the inner and outer `try` blocks use the same `f"... {error.__class__.__name__}[{error.__traceback__.tb_lineno}]: {error}"` pattern. This appears to match existing house style in compute_service.py, so leaving it alone is reasonable — but a one-line helper `_log_gcp_error(logger, context, error)` would shrink every call site and remove the temptation to vary the format. Not blocking; a cleanup for a later pass.

review.summary: The check itself is small and reads cleanly — a straightforward filter over a list of Images. The real problems are in the data layer. `publicly_shared: bool` is the wrong shape: it conflates "not shared" with "we couldn't read the IAM policy," which causes a security scanner to silently return PASS on permission-denied images. The fix is to store the raw `public_members` (or at minimum an `iam_policy_known` flag) and derive the predicate, and to split `_get_images` into three small composable steps (list, fetch policy, classify). Also: pick one canonical check name — the CHANGELOG, PR description, and code currently disagree.
